project.name: novedades_mf
project.description: Microcliente para la gestión, registro, actualización y consulta de novedades poscontractuales de la Universidad Distrital Francisco José de Caldas. Forma parte de la arquitectura de microfrontends del sistema de gestión contractual y se integra en el cliente contenedor mediante single-spa. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: ADR-001-reescritura-angular18.md
nodes.summary: Decides to fully rewrite the legacy AngularJS 1.7.9/Grunt/Bower 'novedades_cliente' module as a new Angular 18 application rather than doing an incremental ngUpgrade migration, since the AngularJS-to-modern-Angular gap makes a hybrid bridge as costly as a rewrite. Only functional behavior is migrated from the gathered legacy requirements, not code; functional parity is tracked explicitly in MIGRATION_PLAN.md, and upgrading Angular further requires an explicit new decision.

nodes.name: ADR-002-parcel-single-spa.md
nodes.summary: Decides to package the app as a single-spa UMD parcel ('novedades-mf') via @angular-builders/custom-webpack + single-spa-angular, per OAS institutional guidelines, instead of Module Federation or iframes. main.single-spa.ts is the sole entry point exporting bootstrap/mount/unmount and auto-bootstraps standalone only via its own index.html; APP_BASE_HREF is '/novedades' and zone.js is excluded from the bundle (provided by the root via CDN). Establishes permanent constraints: no unscoped global styles (see ADR-007), no mat-typography on the root template, and deployUrl-driven chunk resolution (see ADR-010).

nodes.name: ADR-003-standalone-zoneless-signals.md
nodes.summary: Decides to build the whole microfrontend with standalone components, zoneless change detection, and signals as the reactive state model, diverging deliberately from the institutional guide project (solicitudes_sabaticos_mf) which uses NgModules + zone.js. RxJS is reserved for I/O (HTTP, valueChanges); the divergence was validated as an acceptable equivalence in COMPLIANCE_REPORT.md. Derived rule: never depend on zone.js as a patch (e.g. no detectChanges() workaround) — if a view doesn't react, the state wasn't a signal.

nodes.name: ADR-004-ddd-dominio-unico.md
nodes.summary: Decides to organize the codebase as layered DDD within a single domain folder (src/app/domains/contratos/: domain/application/infrastructure/presentation) instead of a flat Angular components/services structure (which repeats the legacy defect of business logic embedded in components) or full tactical DDD (aggregates, domain events, judged over-engineered for current scope). Future domains replicate the same four-layer pattern as sibling folders; shared/ stays outside the layers and holds no business logic. Explicitly forbids adding more DDD concepts without demonstrated need.

nodes.name: ADR-005-repositorio-como-puerto.md
nodes.summary: Decides to model IContractRepository as an abstract class used simultaneously as a DI token and a port, with HttpContractService (real) and MockContractService (dev) as swappable implementations bound in a single line in app.config.ts. All tolerance for the legacy backend's messy, undocumented schema lives in infrastructure/dtos + infrastructure/mappers (anti-corruption layer) — the domain never sees a DTO. Consequence: every new operation must be implemented twice (real and mock), a documented obligation in AI_GUIDE.md.

nodes.name: ADR-006-estado-con-signals.md
nodes.summary: Decides to manage shared UI state (search results, selected contract, loading/error flags) with signals inside application services rather than adopting NgRx (disproportionate ceremony for ~2 state slices) or BehaviorSubject-based services (double reactivity mechanism, clashes with zoneless per ADR-003). Canonical example is ContractStateService: a private signal plus public computed selectors and action methods; RxJS is only a transport converted at the edge. BehaviorSubject as a view store is an explicitly forbidden anti-pattern in CODING_STANDARDS.md.

nodes.name: ADR-007-tailwind-tokens.md
nodes.summary: Decides to style the microfrontend with Tailwind and custom semantic design tokens (the 'Stitch' garnet/gold visual redesign) rather than a full Angular Material theme (would fight the non-Material design) or per-component SCSS (no token system, prone to divergence); Angular Material is kept only where it adds behavior (icons, accessible autocomplete). Tailwind's Preflight reset is disabled because its unscoped global reset leaked into the single-spa shell and broke root elements; an equivalent reset is scoped to the 'novedades-mf' host in styles.css. Permanent rules: never re-enable Preflight, no unscoped global selectors, no new Material surface components.

nodes.name: ADR-008-clase-base-paginas-novedad.md
nodes.summary: Decides to introduce an abstract base class CreateNoveltyPage (a @Directive() for DI support) shared by the five novelty-creation pages (adición/prórroga, suspensión, cesión, terminación, reinicio) so they don't each duplicate the load-contract/breadcrumb/validate/confirm-modal/submit lifecycle. Each page only defines noveltyName, form, buildDraft(), and buildSummary(); visual composition remains component-based. Explicitly documented as an exceptional, deliberate use of inheritance — not a general pattern — and no further component hierarchies should be added without a new ADR.

nodes.name: ADR-009-autenticacion-delegada.md
nodes.summary: Decides that this microfrontend only consumes the OAuth2/WSO2 access token from localStorage rather than implementing its own login flow, preserving the shell's single-session model. auth.interceptor.ts re-reads access_token/id_token/token on every request (supporting shell-driven renewal, unlike the guide project's RequestManager which captures it once) and attaches it only to allowlisted URLs (environment *_SERVICE), preventing token leakage to third parties. dev-token.ts is a temporary local-dev hook that must stay empty in commits. Role-based access control from token contents is deferred to MIG-010 in MIGRATION_PLAN.md.

nodes.name: ADR-010-deployurl-por-ambiente.md
nodes.summary: Fixes a bug where production builds emitted lazy-chunk/asset URLs pointing at localhost:4209 (the shared deployUrl in angular.json) instead of each environment's public single-spa host. Decides to set deployUrl per build configuration to the real public URL (production/test/development), matching the institutional guide project's pattern, rather than deriving the public path at runtime via a generic set-public-path.ts. If deployment hosting changed frequently, the runtime-derivation alternative should be reconsidered via a new ADR.

nodes.name: ADR-011-escrituras-simuladas.md
nodes.summary: Decides on a phased backend integration: connect read endpoints (contracts, providers, novedades) to the real backend immediately, while write operations (create/annul novelty) stay simulated behind HttpContractService (delay(400) + console.warn + TODO(escrituras) markers) until the POST/PATCH payload contract and the Ágora replication mechanism are defined with the backend team. forceError test switches let the UI's error paths be exercised meanwhile. Documented as the #1 production-blocking risk in MIGRATION_PLAN.md. Superseded by ADR-014 once real writes were connected (2026-07-07, closing MIG-001).

nodes.name: ADR-012-regla-mes-30-dias.md
nodes.summary: Decides to preserve the legacy system's fixed 30-days-per-month arithmetic for contract term calculations (DIAS_POR_MES = 30 in format.util.ts's addDaysToTerm) rather than switching to real calendar-month arithmetic, to keep parity with historical actas and the still-live production system. This is explicitly a business/legal decision pending formal ratification (tracked as technical debt TD-010 in MIGRATION_PLAN.md); format.util.ts is the single change point if business later decides otherwise.

nodes.name: ADR-013-normalizacion-fechas-legado.md
nodes.summary: Decides NOT to replicate two legacy date behaviors (normalizing to noon, and auto-correcting day 31 to the 1st of the next month), concluding they were technical workarounds for JavaScript Date/timezone bugs rather than real business rules. The microfrontend's date arithmetic parses yyyy-mm-dd/dd/mm/yyyy strings to local Date objects (format.util.ts#parseAnyDate), where the midnight/UTC offset bug doesn't apply, so only the visible correct result is preserved, not the literal legacy mechanism. Edge cases (Jan 31 + 1 day/month, leap-year Feb) are covered by format.util.spec.ts.

nodes.name: ADR-014-escrituras-reales-sin-replica.md
nodes.summary: Decides to connect real writes to novedades_mid with a minimal documented cascade — validate state transition, create the novelty (novelty-payload.mapper.ts, discriminated by tiponovedad), then register the resulting contract state — deliberately NOT replicating the legacy client's full choreography of replica-to-Ágora plus manual compensation on failure (that transactionality is deferred to the backend as TD-007). Annulment lets the mid revert state in cascade. The mid's {Type, Code, Body} envelope is validated explicitly since it can return HTTP 200 with a business error. Supersedes ADR-011; forceError test switches are kept since there's still no way to exercise UI error paths otherwise. Known accepted risk: without backend-side replication, created novedades are not yet reflected in Titan/preliquidación.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: novedades_mf is an Angular 18 single-spa microfrontend for managing post-contractual "novedades" (contract updates) at Universidad Distrital Francisco José de Caldas: additions, extensions, assignments, suspensions, terminations, and restarts of contracts. The README explains its role inside the larger contract-management microfrontend architecture, how it plugs into a Root/Core shell via single-spa, and how to set up the project locally. Keep this big picture in mind as the tour moves from the shell integration point down into the domain logic that drives every novelty type.

tour.title: Single-Spa Entry Point
tour.description: src/main.single-spa.ts is the true entry point of the application: it wires the Angular lifecycle functions (bootstrap, mount, unmount) that single-spa calls to load, mount, and tear down this microfrontend inside the host shell. It bootstraps AppComponent under the /novedades base href when hosted, or auto-bootstraps standalone for local development. AppComponent itself is the root shell component that renders the routed pages you'll see throughout the tour.
tour.languageLesson: single-spa microfrontends export bootstrap/mount/unmount lifecycle hooks instead of a normal Angular main.ts bootstrapApplication call directly at the top level -- single-spa-angular wraps that call so the host shell controls when this app's DOM gets attached and detached.

tour.title: Application Bootstrap & Routing
tour.description: app.config.ts wires the root providers: routing, an HTTP client with the auth interceptor attached, zoneless change detection, and -- critically -- the DI binding from the IContractRepository port to its concrete HttpContractService implementation. app.routes.ts then defines the lazy-loaded routes for the dashboard and every novelty-creation flow (adición/prórroga, suspensión, cesión, terminación, reinicio, póliza), guarding the creation routes with contractAccessGuard. Together these two files are the map of "what pages exist and what powers them" that the rest of the tour fills in.

tour.title: Domain Model: Contracts & Novelties
tour.description: The domain layer is framework-free TypeScript describing the business vocabulary: contract.entity.ts models a contract, contract-status.enum.ts enumerates its lifecycle states, novelty-type.enum.ts enumerates the six kinds of novelty this app can create, and novelty-draft.model.ts captures the in-progress form data for each novelty type before submission. docs/DOMAIN.md explains the same concepts in business terms -- contracts, contractors, and why each novelty type exists -- giving you the "why" behind the types you just read. Everything downstream (repositories, mappers, pages) speaks in terms of these models.

tour.title: Domain Business Rules
tour.description: contract.rules.ts is the highest fan-in and fan-out file in the codebase -- it encodes the actual business logic: which contract statuses allow which novelty types, and date-normalization rules carried over from the legacy system. Because it's pure, framework-free TypeScript operating only on the models from Step 4, it can be unit-tested in isolation and reused identically by both presentation pages and infrastructure mappers. This is the module every novelty-creation page ultimately defers to when deciding whether an action is legal.
tour.languageLesson: Keeping business rules as plain exported functions operating on plain interfaces/enums (no Angular decorators, no framework imports) is what makes this layer framework-free DDD -- it can be tested and reasoned about without spinning up Angular's DI or change detection.

tour.title: Repository Port & Infrastructure Adapter
tour.description: contract.repository.ts is an abstract class acting as both a DI token and a port (ADR-005) -- the domain layer depends only on this interface, never on HTTP details. HttpContractService is the real implementation, translating calls into requests against the legacy backend; legacy-api.dto.ts mirrors that backend's raw, undocumented shapes, and contract.mapper.ts / novelty-payload.mapper.ts form the anti-corruption layer that converts between those DTOs and the clean domain models from Step 4. This indirection is what let the app swap in a mock implementation during development without touching a single domain or presentation file.
tour.languageLesson: Modeling a repository as an abstract class rather than a TypeScript interface lets Angular's DI system use the class itself as an injection token -- interfaces disappear at runtime, but abstract classes don't, so `providers: [{ provide: IContractRepository, useClass: HttpContractService }]` works directly.

tour.title: Shared Novelty-Creation Lifecycle
tour.description: Rather than duplicating the load-contract/validate/confirm/submit/retry flow across five near-identical pages, create-novelty-page.base.ts introduces an abstract base class (ADR-008) that each novelty page extends, overriding only noveltyName, form, buildDraft(), and buildSummary(). confirm-novelty-modal.component.ts is the shared confirmation dialog this base class opens before calling the repository from Step 6. This is documented as a deliberate, exceptional use of inheritance -- not a pattern to replicate elsewhere in the codebase.
tour.languageLesson: An abstract class decorated with @Directive() (rather than @Component()) lets Angular still perform dependency injection into it, even though it's never instantiated or rendered directly -- only its concrete subclasses are.

tour.title: The Five Novelty-Creation Pages
tour.description: These are the five concrete novelty-creation pages, each extending the base class from Step 7: adición/prórroga (extending a contract's term), suspensión (pausing it), cesión (reassigning it to a new contractor), terminación (ending it early), and reinicio (resuming after a suspension, computing the resumed term from the prior suspension period). Each page's job is narrow -- define its own form and how to build a NoveltyDraft and a human-readable summary -- because the shared lifecycle, validation, and submission mechanics already live in CreateNoveltyPage.

tour.title: Contract Dashboard
tour.description: dashboard-contratos.component.ts is the landing page of the application: a search/filter form for contracts, the resulting contract list, and workflows for annulling a novelty or activating a contract. It's the highest fan-out presentation page after the novelty pages, exercising the same repository port and contract rules from Steps 5-6 but for read and state-transition operations rather than novelty creation. This is typically the first page a user actually sees after logging in through the shell.

tour.title: Shared UI Building Blocks
tour.description: form-field.component.ts, form-input.directive.ts, and card.component.ts are presentation-agnostic Angular Material building blocks reused across every novelty page and the dashboard from Steps 8-9. Keeping them outside the contratos domain folder (in shared/ui) means they carry no business logic and could be reused if a second domain were ever added alongside contratos, per the single-domain DDD boundary established in ADR-004.

tour.title: Cross-Cutting Auth & Session
tour.description: This microfrontend never implements its own login: user-session.service.ts decodes the JWT the single-spa shell already deposited in localStorage to read roles/documento/email, auth.interceptor.ts re-reads that token on every HTTP request and attaches it only to allowlisted institutional API URLs, and contract-access.guard.ts (used by the routes in Step 3) restricts a SUPERVISOR-only user to contracts they actually supervise. dev-token.ts is a local-dev-only escape hatch for testing without running the shell's OAuth flow, and must stay empty in real commits -- a known, documented risk if that rule is ever broken.
tour.languageLesson: Angular's functional HTTP interceptors (a plain function passed to `withInterceptors`) replaced the older class-based HttpInterceptor pattern in Angular 15+, fitting naturally with this project's standalone, provider-function-based bootstrap in app.config.ts.

tour.title: Architecture Decisions
tour.description: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md ties every layer from this tour together in one document: the DDD layering, the layer-dependency rules, and how a novelty gets created end to end. The four linked ADRs record why each major structural decision was made: ADR-004 justifies the single-domain DDD folder structure from Steps 4-9, ADR-005 justifies the repository-as-port pattern from Step 6, ADR-008 justifies the base-class inheritance from Step 7, and ADR-014 documents the most recent change -- connecting real backend writes (superseding an earlier simulated-writes decision) with a minimal validate-create-register cascade. Reading these last turns everything you just saw from "how it works" into "why it was built this way."
